neighbours.label: ' as' right after a passive attribution or reputation verb (quoted as, credited as, noted as, regarded as); not comparative or role 'as'
fire: The senator is frequently quoted as an opponent of the treaty.
The chemist is generally credited as the discoverer of the element.
The harbour town is mainly noted as the birthplace of a famous poet.
The painting is widely regarded as the finest work of the period.
In the minutes she is cited as the author of the proposal.
The old mill is commonly described as the heart of the village.
The general is usually remembered as a cautious commander.
The valley is often mentioned as a refuge for rare birds.
quiet: The senator served as an opponent of the treaty for two terms.
The chemist spent ten years as an assistant in the laboratory.
As the tide went out, the harbour town fell silent.
The painting is almost as large as the wall behind it.
In the minutes she wrote the proposal down as soon as it was read.
The old mill is now used as a village library.
The general was not as cautious as his rivals.
The valley floods as the snow melts each spring.

notes: Card: ' as' x15 after quoted/credited/noted, plus ' stated', 'rec|ited'. Probes: noted as 0.85, quoted as 0.59, credited as 0.51; 'worked as' 0.04, 'As the sun' 0.03, 'as tall as' 0.02. Low-magnitude pole (max 3.56, 40% echo regime).
